content.overview: Mastering the inflection and tense agreements of verbs according to subject number, person, voice, modals, and conditional clauses.
key_terms: Subject-Verb Agreement: A singular subject requires a singular verb; a plural subject requires a plural verb.
Conditionals: Zero, First, Second, and Third conditionals governing verb forms in dependent clauses.
Gerund vs Infinitive: Verb + ing acting as a noun vs 'to' + base form.
study_notes: With 'as well as', 'along with', 'together with', the verb agrees with the first subject.
With 'neither...nor' or 'either...or', the verb agrees with the closer subject.
After modal auxiliaries (can, could, may, might, shall, should, will, would, must), use base form.

mcqs.content: Neither the teacher nor the students ______ present in the auditorium. A. was B. were C. is D. has been Answer: B
The captain, along with his team members, ______ received warmly by the principal. A. were B. was C. are D. have been Answer: B
If I ______ a bird, I would fly in the sky. A. was B. were C. am D. have been Answer: B
It is high time we ______ our corrupt practices. A. change B. changed C. had changed D. will change Answer: B
He talks as if he ______ everything. A. knows B. knew C. has known D. knowing Answer: B
Scarcely had the teacher entered the classroom ______ the students stood up. A. when B. than C. then D. after Answer: A
No sooner had we reached the station ______ the train left. A. when B. than C. then D. before Answer: B
I look forward to ______ from you soon. A. hear B. hearing C. heard D. have heard Answer: B
You had better ______ a doctor without delay. A. to see B. see C. saw D. seeing Answer: B
One of my closest friends ______ living in Canada for five years. A. are B. has been C. have been D. were Answer: B
Walk briskly lest you ______ miss the morning train. A. will B. can C. should D. would Answer: C
Fifty miles ______ a long distance to travel on foot. A. is B. are C. were D. have been Answer: A
The jury ______ unanimous in their verdict. A. was B. were C. is D. has been Answer: A
He prevented me from ______ into the examination hall without an admit card. A. enter B. entering C. to enter D. entered Answer: B
If you had studied diligently, you ______ passed the board examination. A. will have B. would have C. would D. could Answer: B
The news published in yesterday's newspaper ______ truly shocking. A. were B. was C. are D. have been Answer: B
She made her younger brother ______ his homework before dinner. A. finish B. to finish C. finished D. finishing Answer: A
Bread and butter ______ his favourite breakfast everyday. A. is B. are C. were D. have been Answer: A
Had I possessed the required funds, I ______ helped the impoverished students. A. would have B. will have C. should D. must Answer: A
I would rather starve than ______ stolen food. A. to eat B. eat C. ate D. eating Answer: B

content.answer_tip: Check proximity rules for either/or and memorize past subjunctive forms for 'as if' and 'wish'.

content.overview: Standard idiomatic and contextual prepositions governing verbs, adjectives, and noun collocations in NCTB examinations.
key_terms: Appropriate Preposition: Conventional pairing of prepositions with particular adjectives, verbs, or nouns (e.g., absorbed in, addicted to).
Phrasal Verbs: Combinations of verb + preposition carrying idiomatic meaning.
study_notes: Senior, junior, superior, inferior take 'to', never 'than'.
Congratulate takes 'on', abstain takes 'from', prevent takes 'from'.

mcqs.content: He is senior ______ me by three years in academic service. A. than B. to C. from D. with Answer: B
We congratulated the student ______ his outstanding GPA-5 achievement. A. for B. on C. at D. in Answer: B
A pious person always abstains ______ speaking ill of others. A. of B. from C. with D. to Answer: B
He died ______ dengue fever after fighting for a week in hospital. A. of B. from C. by D. for Answer: A
The patriot died ______ his motherland during the war of independence. A. of B. for C. by D. through Answer: B
She is proficient ______ English grammar and communicative vocabulary. A. at B. in C. with D. for Answer: B
The young man is addicted ______ playing mobile video games late at night. A. for B. to C. with D. on Answer: B
Smoking is harmful ______ human lungs and cardiovascular health. A. for B. to C. with D. at Answer: B
The judge found the accused guilty ______ criminal misappropriation. A. with B. of C. for D. about Answer: B
We should abide ______ the traffic regulations strictly on highways. A. with B. by C. to D. for Answer: B
He aimed his arrow ______ the target in archery practice. A. on B. at C. to D. towards Answer: B
The doctor advised the patient to refrain ______ smoking cigarettes. A. of B. from C. to D. off Answer: B
I am accustomed ______ waking up early at dawn. A. with B. to C. for D. on Answer: B
The committee consists ______ five esteemed senior professors. A. in B. of C. with D. by Answer: B
He boasts ______ his wealthy family inheritance. A. for B. of C. on D. at Answer: B
Water is composed ______ hydrogen and oxygen molecules. A. by B. of C. with D. in Answer: B
Are you confident ______ scoring the highest marks in this examination? A. in B. of C. at D. on Answer: B
He is blind ______ his son's obvious misconduct and faults. A. of B. to C. with D. in Answer: B
The beggar is blind ______ his left eye since childhood. A. of / in B. to C. for D. at Answer: A
You must compensate ______ the financial damage you caused to the school laboratory. A. with B. for C. at D. on Answer: B

content.answer_tip: Note: die of a disease; die for a noble cause; blind to a fault; blind in/of an eye.

content.overview: Sentence enhancement using pre-modifiers, post-modifiers, determiners, participle phrases, and logical connectors.
key_terms: Pre-modifier: Word or phrase appearing before a noun to clarify or specify its meaning.
Post-modifier: Descriptive element appearing after a noun or verb (e.g., prepositional phrase, relative clause).
Connectors: Transitional words establishing cause, contrast, sequence, or addition.
study_notes: Present participle (V-ing) modifier denotes active action; past participle denotes completed/passive state.

mcqs.content: In 'The barking dog rarely bites', the word 'barking' functions as a: A. Post-modifier B. Pre-modifier participle C. Relative clause D. Conjunction Answer: B
Which connector expresses a direct logical contrast? A. Furthermore B. However C. Consequently D. In addition Answer: B
He studied diligently; ______, he topped the board examination. A. nevertheless B. therefore C. on the contrary D. whereas Answer: B
In 'Kazi Nazrul Islam, our national poet, wrote rebel poems', 'our national poet' is an: A. Appositive B. Infinitive C. Adverbial clause D. Gerund Answer: A
Which connector is best to introduce an additional complementary point? A. Moreover B. Although C. In spite of D. Otherwise Answer: A
In 'The boy standing near the door is my cousin', 'standing near the door' is a: A. Pre-modifier B. Post-modifier participle phrase C. Noun clause D. Adverbial phrase Answer: B
______ he was physically exhausted, he continued working to meet the deadline. A. Because B. Although C. Since D. Therefore Answer: B
Water pollution is increasing; ______, aquatic life is facing grave danger. A. as a result B. nevertheless C. whereas D. on the other hand Answer: A
In 'He bought a gold watch', the word 'gold' is a: A. Noun used as an adjective pre-modifier B. Adverb C. Pronoun D. Gerund Answer: A
You must hurry; ______, you will miss the morning departure. A. consequently B. otherwise C. furthermore D. likewise Answer: B
In 'She spoke very softly', the word 'very' functions as an: A. Intensifier adverb pre-modifying an adverb B. Adjective C. Conjunction D. Preposition Answer: A
______ honest he is, he is not arrogant about his virtue. A. Though B. As C. Yet D. Since Answer: A
Which word is an example of a demonstrative determiner used as a pre-modifier? A. These B. Some C. Quick D. Often Answer: A
In 'I saw the girl singing melodiously', 'singing melodiously' modifies: A. I B. the girl C. saw D. none Answer: B
He worked hard ______ he could pass the medical entrance exam. A. in order that / so that B. lest C. unless D. whereas Answer: A
Smoking is harmful to lungs; ______, it wastes valuable hard-earned money. A. besides B. but C. however D. although Answer: A
In 'A rolling stone gathers no moss', 'rolling' is a: A. Present participle pre-modifier B. Gerund C. Infinitive D. Adverb Answer: A
The weather was hostile; ______, our flight departed on schedule. A. consequently B. nonetheless / nevertheless C. as a result D. therefore Answer: B
In 'The book on the table belongs to Rahim', 'on the table' is a: A. Prepositional phrase post-modifier B. Pre-modifier C. Conjunction D. Predicate Answer: A
______ honesty is the best policy, dishonest people briefly thrive through corruption. A. While / Although B. Therefore C. Because D. Moreover Answer: A

content.answer_tip: Look at connector direction: Addition (Moreover), Contrast (However, Nonetheless), Cause & Effect (Therefore, Consequently).
